title: Gregory Herbert's discipline and how he joined
summary: Herman calls Herbert the most disciplined young player in years; Wong relays that Richie Cole had heard him in Atlantic City before he joined on tenor.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Uh-huh.

And as I said, many years later, when I tried to describe to Charlotte or anyone else how I felt about Gregory, Gregory's playing, in a way, he was the most disciplined young player I'd heard in many a year.
Uh-huh.
And that to me is a high compliment.
And he came from rather a mixed --
Bag.
-- bag of learning and so forth.
Yeah. He studied many different actions.
He was from Philadelphia.
Yes, he did. And he had a good small group, just prior to joining you, too, I heard.
Who's this, now, you're speaking of?
Gregory.
He had a small group?

Small group, before he joined you. Let's see, who told me that? Yeah, Richie Cole, the young alto player. Told me when Richie was with Buddy Rich's band, and he was out there in Atlanta City, and he heard Gregory Herbert playing the alto, and he wrote + said, 'Boy, listen to that guy, wow, that's what I want to do.' And I think he said, two or three days after -- several years with Buddy, he left, and did that. And he says, 'Ironically, Gregory joined Woody Herman.'
On tenor?
On tenor, yeah.
But, anyway, looking at it from this aspect, of -- what I was trying to state was that only certain players had this maturity (inaudible) that early in life.
It's a gift.
To some degree I think it is, yeah. And maybe another kid would say, 'Well, I don't ever want to be like that.'
Uh-huh.
But I think it's very important if you want to grow a long career, if that's what you seek (inaudible).
